chunks: And al-Shaykh — may God support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from 'Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from his father, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad [variant: Ghawwad], from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say:
'Whoever falls asleep while bowing, prostrating, or walking — in whatever state — wudu is obligatory upon him.'

key_terms.الْحَالَاتِ: states, conditions — the generalising term covering all postures and circumstances
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu, the ritual ablution obligatory before salat and other acts of worship
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: one bowing in ruku', the inclined posture in salat
key_terms.سَاجِدٌ: one prostrating in sajda, the full prostration of salat

ai.seo_question: Does falling asleep in ruku', sajda, or while walking nullify wudu according to Shia hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a comprehensive ruling that sleep nullifies wudu without exception, regardless of the bodily position at the time of sleeping — whether in ruku', sajda, or walking. The phrase 'in whatever state' (عَلَى أَيِّ الْحَالَاتِ) serves as a legal generalisation, closing any possible exception based on posture or circumstance.
